clue.text: Sort of service tree variety

parts.note: the willow is a tree
a pattern is a design or variety, as of fabric or china

explanation.surface: Someone names a particular strain of tree, perhaps a rowan, known as the service tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service tree' is a real tree, which tempts a reading as one unit; here 'service' belongs to the definition, a set of china.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow pattern is a famous blue-and-white Chinese-style design on dinner sets, so it names a kind of china service.

clue.text: Dispute over vessel for ritual

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned over, so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a row is a dispute
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: Two parties argue about which boat to use in a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal religious observance or devotion is a ritual act of reverence.

clue.text: Working far away, virtually solo, on big house

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so first
virtually means almost, so the word for solo loses its final letter

parts.note: lone means solo, alone
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: Someone works remotely, almost on their own, from a country mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range weapons or flights operate over great distances.

clue.text: Love good actor appearing as old characters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: An affectionate, decent performer turns up as a group of period figures in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in a play, but here it means letters: an ancient Celtic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an early Irish script of strokes, so its letters are ancient written symbols.

clue.text: Take pawn or suffer in opening on board

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
taken as written
thole is an old Scots and northern word meaning to endure or suffer

explanation.surface: A chess player decides whether to capture a pawn or endure a weak start to the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' and 'board' suggest chess, but the board is a ship's deck and the opening a round window.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's round window is a gap in its side, aboard the vessel.

clue.text: Do defeat decisively

definitions.meaning: a do or a ... is British slang for a lively party

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to win by a wide margin.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a party is a do, and a crushing win is a thrashing.

clue.text: Site meant for rebuilding cafe

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are torn down and built up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A plot of land is earmarked for constructing a coffee shop again.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe or bar.

clue.text: Material that's new — only out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the following word's letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fabric is fresh and exclusively on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric used for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Laughed to see fish hiding in river bottom

indicators.note: one piece hides by sitting inside another, which wraps it

parts.note: a river bed is the bottom of a river
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone chuckles at spotting a fish concealed in the mud of a riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Brayed means laughed loudly and harshly, like a donkey's cry.

clue.text: He keeps a range of stock

definitions.text: He keeps a range of stock

parts.words: He keeps a range of stock
parts.note: reads like a shopkeeper with a wide inventory, but the stock is cattle and the range is open grazing land

explanation.surface: A retailer carries a wide inventory of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle farmer keeps livestock on open grazing country in the American West.

clue.text: Fine specimen of snake

definitions.meaning: in dated British slang a ... is something excellent, a cracker

explanation.surface: Someone admires a splendid example of a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is old slang for a first-rate thing and short for the venomous American snake with a rattling tail.

clue.text: Part of Muslim household in East needing damage limitation

indicators.note: the abbreviation for East goes in, framed by the word for damage

parts.note: harm is damage
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A family in the East wants to keep its losses down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing damage limitation' sounds like insurance talk; 'limitation' suggests the E sits within the limits of the word for damage.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a traditional Muslim home.

clue.text: No speech is worth this amount

definitions.text: No speech is worth this amount

parts.words: No speech is worth this amount
parts.note: sounds like a sneer at oratory, but means a payment made to keep someone silent

explanation.surface: A critic says no speech could ever deserve such a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe paid to buy someone's silence is what you pay for no speech.

clue.text: Write chapter in story that makes five points

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: the chapter abbreviation is put inside the word for story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An author adds a chapter to a story that scores five points.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentacle is a five-pointed star used as a magic symbol.

clue.text: Attractive, so asking out?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, fielders appeal to the umpire, asking for a batsman to be given out

explanation.surface: Someone attractive wonders whether to ask a date out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'asking out' looks like requesting a date; cricket's appeal, the shout of 'Howzat?', asks the umpire to give the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive things please or charm, and a fielder's shout to the umpire is an appeal.

clue.text: Girl's name to enter here

definitions.meaning: a female first name, Scandinavian in origin
read as two words, where the solver writes answers, in the crossword's squares

explanation.surface: A form asks for a girl's name to be written in this space.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a girl's name, and split it says the answer goes in the grid.

clue.text: Remove from Oxford, to avoid a smooth finish?

definitions.meaning: to send a student away from university for a time as a punishment
in masonry, rustication gives stonework a rough-hewn surface rather than a smooth one

explanation.surface: An Oxford student is sent down, perhaps for refusing to polish their work.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities suspend students by sending them down, and stonemasons give blocks a roughened face.

clue.text: Italian entitled to study investment

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a TESSA was a Tax-Exempt Special Savings Account, a British savings scheme of the 1990s

explanation.surface: An Italian aristocrat reads up on where to put her money.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a woman with a noble title.

clue.text: In spring, woman's planted Asian climber

indicators.note: the woman's word is placed inside the word for a spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
her is the possessive of a woman

explanation.surface: In springtime, a woman has planted an Asian climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted' supports the insertion; 'climber' suggests a plant in the garden picture, but it is a Himalayan mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters.

clue.text: Purchaser, moneyed; secures this good address

indicators.note: the words hold the answer fast inside them, spanning the comma

explanation.surface: A wealthy buyer gets hold of this fine house address.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a moral address delivered from the pulpit.

clue.text: Argues about expenses, grabbing note nonetheless

indicators.note: the word for expenses takes hold of the trimmed word inside it

parts.note: costs are expenses

indicators.note: read as none less, the word note loses its O, its nothing

explanation.surface: Someone disputes expenses while still seizing a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' looks like an adverb meaning 'still', but split as 'none less' it tells you to drop the O, a zero or nothing, from the word note.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or challenge a claim is to argue against it.

clue.text: Unknown amount in cut fowl — indicate how much you want

indicators.note: the unknown quantity is placed inside the word for cut

parts.note: to saw is to cut
in algebra Y stands for an unknown quantity
a hen is a domestic fowl

explanation.surface: A carver asks how much chicken a guest would like.
explanation.definitionFit: A pourer or server asks the guest to signal when enough has been given.

clue.text: Cheerful pub cooking — tuck in

indicators.note: cooking means messing with, so these three letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: to tuck in is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: A pub serves food and the customers dig in happily.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means optimistic and in good spirits.

clue.text: Rolls lined up for distinguished visitor

definitions.text: Rolls lined up for distinguished visitor

parts.words: Rolls lined up for distinguished visitor
parts.note: suggests Rolls-Royces queued for a VIP, but means a ceremonial carpet unrolled for an honoured guest

explanation.surface: A fleet of Rolls-Royces waits in line to collect a VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A crimson strip laid out for celebrities marks a special welcome.

clue.text: Given group of workers to use in hydroelectric project

indicators.note: the workers' group is placed inside the project, to work there

parts.note: a dam generates hydroelectric power
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A union crew is brought in to work on a hydroelectric scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a fact taken as given, from the Latin for something given.

clue.text: Roman writer given place in history at last

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word history is used

explanation.surface: A Roman author finally earns a place in the history books.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliny the Elder and his nephew Pliny the Younger were Roman authors.

clue.text: Predatory team shot in exercise

indicators.note: the word for shot of goes inside the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
shot of means rid of

explanation.surface: A predatory squad is gunned down during training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is from 'get shot of', British slang for get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions, hunting together, is called a pride.

clue.text: Sketch rugby formation back to front

indicators.note: the back part of the word is brought round to the front

parts.note: a lineout is the rugby set piece when the ball is thrown in from touch

explanation.surface: A coach draws a rugby set play from rear to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough drawing showing only the main lines.

clue.text: Popeye's favourite ship can, at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cartoon sailor's beloved vessel holds tins out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Popeye is the cartoon sailor who eats canned greens for strength; 'ship' and 'at sea' fit his world.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor gulps tinned leafy greens to gain strength.

clue.text: Was perhaps an underachiever

definitions.meaning: expressing a possibility in the past
a person who failed to fulfil their promise

explanation.surface: Someone who perhaps did not live up to expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses past possibility, and as a noun it names someone who never fulfilled their promise.
